Drawing textbook horizontal support and resistance lines looks simple in retrospect, but modern algorithmic market microstructure makes it a retail liquidity trap.

Static horizontal lines ignore institutional order-flow mechanics and algorithmic liquidity sweeps. In modern electronic markets dominated by high-frequency trading (HFT) and institutional algorithms, visible retail support and resistance levels are frequently target zones for liquidity sweeps—triggering retail stop-loss clusters before reversing. Relying on basic textbook chart patterns without understanding volume profile, delta, or Greeks leads to persistent false breakouts.

Stop treating textbook chart lines like crystal balls. Consistent trading edge comes from understanding institutional liquidity and position sizing, not visual pattern projection.

— PaisaFactCheck
